public_rationale: The evidence is consistent with continued reasoning, safety, and hallucination problems, and it also documents meaningful gains from scaling. However, the reviewed frontier models combine pretraining with architecture changes, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or tools. Their results do not isolate the pretraining-only assertion across all three named problems. Under the stated criteria, that evidence gap prevents a supported or contradicted outcome.
limitations: This is an evidence limitation, not evidence that pretraining alone had solved the problems.
A looser assessment of deployed-model reliability would have stronger support, but would omit the explicit word alone.
Current failures would not establish a permanent theoretical limit on scaling.

our_interpretation: Assess the present-status assertion that pretraining scale alone had not solved the three named problems, rather than whether Marcus previously made the argument.
Solved means reliable handling across relevant tasks, not merely better average benchmark scores.
This does not claim that future pretraining scale can never solve these problems.
The word alone requires evidence distinguishing pretraining from post-training, tools, and other interventions.
Use current-year evaluations through the post date, since technical evaluations have no common quarterly reporting cycle.
